problem: Vertices \( A, B, C \) of an equilateral triangle with side length 1 are on the surface of a sphere with radius 1 and center \( O \). Let \( D \) be the orthogonal projection of \( A \) onto the plane \( \alpha \) determined by points \( B, C, O \). Let \( N \) be one of the intersections of the line perpendicular to \( \alpha \) passing through \( O \) with the sphere. Find the angle \( \angle DNO \).

answer_text:
# Finding Angle ∠DNO

## Setting Up Coordinates

I place **O** at the origin. Since the equilateral triangle ABC (side 1) has circumradius $R_{\text{tri}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, the distance from O to the plane of ABC is:

$$h = \sqrt{1 - \frac{1}{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}$$

Choosing the plane of ABC at $z = h$:

$$A = \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\; 0,\; \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\right), \quad B = \left(-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}},\; \frac{1}{2},\; \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\right), \quad C = \left(-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}},\; -\frac{1}{2},\; \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\right)$$

## Finding Plane α (through B, C, O)

Using vectors $\vec{BC} = (0,-1,0)$ and $\vec{BO} = \left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}, -\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\right)$:

$$\vec{n} = \vec{BC} \times \vec{BO} = \left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3},\; 0,\; \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\right)$$

The plane through O has equation: $z = -2\sqrt{2}\,x$

## Computing D (Projection of A onto α)

$$D = A - \frac{\vec{n}\cdot A}{|\vec{n}|^2}\,\vec{n}$$

With $\vec{n}\cdot A = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $|\vec{n}|^2 = \frac{3}{4}$:

$$D = \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{9},\; 0,\; \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{9}\right)$$

## Finding N (Intersection of normal line with sphere)

The unit normal to α is:

$$\hat{n} = \frac{\vec{n}}{|\vec{n}|} = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3},\; 0,\; \frac{1}{3}\right)$$

So $N = \hat{n}$ (or $-\hat{n}$):

$$N = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3},\; 0,\; \frac{1}{3}\right)$$

## Computing Angle ∠DNO

**Vectors from N:**

$$\vec{ND} = D - N = \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}+6\sqrt{2}}{9},\; 0,\; \frac{2\sqrt{6}-3}{9}\right)$$

$$\vec{NO} = O - N = \left(-\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3},\; 0,\; -\frac{1}{3}\right)$$

**Magnitudes:**

$$|\vec{NO}| = 1, \qquad |\vec{ND}|^2 = \frac{(\sqrt{3}+6\sqrt{2})^2 + (2\sqrt{6}-3)^2}{81} = \frac{(75+12\sqrt{6})+(33-12\sqrt{6})}{81} = \frac{108}{81} = \frac{4}{3}$$

So $|\vec{ND}| = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$.

**Dot product:**

$$\vec{ND}\cdot\vec{NO} = \frac{6\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{3}+6\sqrt{2})}{81} - \frac{3(2\sqrt{6}-3)}{81} = \frac{6\sqrt{6}+72-6\sqrt{6}+9}{81} = 1$$

**The angle:**

$$\cos\angle DNO = \frac{\vec{ND}\cdot\vec{NO}}{|\vec{ND}|\,|\vec{NO}|} = \frac{1}{\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot 1} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$

$$\boxed{\angle DNO = 30°}$$

27B·v4.method: Coordinate geometry: place O at origin, compute vertices, find plane normal via cross product, project A onto plane, find N on sphere, compute angle via dot product.
